{{Quote|THIS ''IS'' A FREIGHTER, YOU KNOW.|AG-37|<ref name="Legacy 3" />}}
A '''freighter''' was owned by [[AG-37]], an [[IG-series/Legends|IG-series]] [[Droid/Legends|droid]] who made a living by transporting goods, between [[138 ABY|138]] and [[140 ABY]]. As a [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]], it did not boast a very fast top speed and could not outrun [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]]. AG-37 served as the main transport vessel for AG-37 and his friends the [[Junk dealer/Legends|junk dealer]] [[Ania Solo]], the [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] [[Engineer/Legends|engineer]] [[Sauk]], and the [[Imperial Knight]] [[Jao Assam]] during the rogue [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Darth Wredd]]'s [[Darth Wredd's insurgency|insurgency]] against the [[Galactic Federation Triumvirate]], the new galactic government, and the [[One Sith]] order. AG-37's freighter participated in several of the group's adventures including the [[Carreras Incident]], the [[Liberation of Mon Calamari Shipyards|liberation]] of the [[Mon Calamari Orbital Shipyards]], Jao and Ania's mission to hunt down Darth Wredd, and a mission to rescue Ania from several kidnappers. During these adventures, AG-37's freighter was damaged several times and escaped destruction on a few occasions.

==Characteristics==
[[File:AG-37_freighter_escapes_tentacled_monster.jpg|thumb|left|250px|AG-37's freighter survived numerous adventures]]
AG-37's freighter was a large, lengthy capital ship that was capable of interstellar travel. As a [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]], it did not boast a very fast top speed and could not outrun [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]].<ref name="Legacy 3" /> However, the freighter was armed with a [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannon]] turret to protect it against enemy starships.<ref name="Legacy 10" /> In addition, the turret was also equipped with a [[Power harpoon launcher|harpoon and tow cable]] that allowed it to retrieve objects. The freighter was capable of transporting various types of cargo including a dangerous [[Unidentified creature (AG-37)|large beast]], which had to be stored in a special cage, and even a squad of [[Trandoshan/Legends|Trandoshan]] [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]].<ref name="Legacy 7">[[Legacy (2013) 7|''Legacy'' (2013) 7]]</ref><ref name="Legacy 16">[[Legacy (2013) 16|''Legacy'' (2013) 16]]</ref> The freighter's hold was also large enough to transport a small starship like [[Ania Solo's starship]] and the Imperial Knight [[Jao Assam]]'s [[Unidentified Galactic Triumvirate starfighter|starfighter]].<ref name="Legacy 3" /> AG-37's freighter was also capable of diving underwater, as shown when AG-37 and Sauk rescued Ania and Jao's [[Escape pod/Legends|escape pod]] from the poisoned oceans of [[Dac/Legends|Dac]].<ref name="Legacy 9" /> It also boasted a small medical bay.<ref name="Legacy 5">[[Legacy (2013) 5|''Legacy'' (2013) 5]]</ref>

==History==
[[File:AG37-Legacy2013-2.jpg|thumb|right|150px|AG-37, the freighter's captain]]

===AG-37's service===
Little is known about the history of AG-37's freighter. Near the end of the [[Second Imperial Civil War]], AG-37 encountered [[Ania Solo]], a distant descendant of the [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], in the [[Selvatas system]]. Ania had escaped from an Imperial labor camp on [[Drash-So]] and was desperate to get offworld. Despite Ania pulling a gun on him, AG-37 took pity on her and gave her passage offworld on his freighter, thus honoring his ancient promise to Han Solo. He brought Ania to [[Carreras Minor's moon]] in the [[Carreras system/Legends|Carreras system]], where she established a [[Ania Solo's junkyard|junkyard]]. As a result of this encounter, AG-37 and Ania became friends.<ref name="Legacy 12">[[Legacy (2013) 12|''Legacy'' (2013) 12]]</ref> AG-37 was also known to visit her junkyard to obtain spare parts for his freighter.<ref name="Legacy 2" />

===The Carreras Incident===
In [[138 ABY]], AG-37 visited Ania Solo's junkyard on Carreras Minor's moon to obtain a pair of linear converters. While visiting the junkyard, Ania and her [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] friend [[Sauk]] were attacked by the rogue Sith [[Darth Wredd]], who was posing as [[Imperial Knight]] [[Yalta Val]]. After escaping Wredd and the Carreras security forces, AG-37's freighter fled into space only to encounter a blockade of [[Carreras starfighter]]s.<ref name="Legacy 2">[[Legacy (2013) 2|''Legacy'' (2013) 2]]</ref> AG-37 took his [[Starship/Legends|ship]] into the rings of [[Carreras Minor]] and Solo jettisoned her ship from the cargo hold, which collided with their pursuers and allowed them to land on-world. The Imperial Knight [[Jao Assam]] then saved the freighter from the clutches of a [[Unidentified Carreras Minor tentacled serpent|tentacled serpent]] and joined the group. After determining that the real Yalta Val had been replaced by an impostor, AG-37's freighter traveled to the floating world of [[Mala (planet)|Mala]], hoping to rescue Master Val. While traveling through the [[Surd Nebula/Legends|Surd Nebula]], they were attacked by several Carreras starfighters. Upon arriving at Mala's last known coordinates, they found that the floating world had vanished. During this pursuit, the freighter sustained damaged to one of its rear thrusters. Shortly later, AG-37's freighter was captured by the [[Tractor beam projector/Legends|tractor beam projector]] of a [[Shifalan patrol ship]].<ref name="Legacy 3" />

AG-37's freighter was then dragged into the hangar bay of the patrol ship where a swarm of tiny droids burnt a hole through its hull and boarded the vessel, driving its crew and passengers down the landing ramp where they were apprehended by Carreras security forces. The freighter and its captive crew were then transported to the [[Carreras G51 communications array]]. Later, Jao, Ania, and their companions were released by the [[Shifala]] [[Governor/Legends|Governor]] [[Biala]] in order to deal with the Sith impostor Darth Wredd. During the skirmish, AG-37, Sauk, and Jao were gravely injured and Wredd managed to escape back to his base on Mala.<ref name="Legacy 4">[[Legacy (2013) 4|''Legacy'' (2013) 4]]</ref> Prior to the destruction of the Carreras communications array which collided with Mala during the "[[Carreras Incident]]," Ania managed to rescue Sauk, AG-37, and Yalta Val, whom she had saved from being killed by Darth Wredd. Jao was rescued by Val's [[Unidentified Imperial communications droid|communications droid]]. However, Darth Wredd managed to escape again for parts unknown.<ref name="Legacy 5" />

===Stopping Darth Luft===
[[File:Sauk_firing_harpoon_gun.jpg|thumb|left|350x|Sauk firing the freighter's harpoon gun]]
The damaged ship was unable to make [[Lightspeed/Legends|lightspeed]], but it was picked up by the ''[[Animus]]'', a [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] affiliated with the [[Galactic Federation Triumvirate]]. Following repairs, AG-37 and Sauk took leave of their friends and left the [[Destroyer/Legends|Destroyer]] to continue with AG-37's transport business.<ref name="Legacy 6">[[Legacy (2013) 6|''Legacy'' (2013) 6]]</ref> After transporting a large beast to [[Iego/Legends|Iego]],<ref name="Legacy 7" /> they later took the freighter to the [[Poison/Legends|poisoned]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] of Dac to aid Solo and Assam, whose communications droid was broadcasting a [[Distress signal/Legends|distress signal]]. In the freighter, AG-37 and Sauk dispatched several [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] ships; they also took their vessel into the world's [[Ocean/Legends|oceans]] and rescued their friends' sinking escape pod with a harpoon and tow cable. Their attempts to flee the [[Mon Calamari system/Legends|system]] led to a run-in with a large pirate [[Fleet/Legends|armada]], but the [[Liberation of Mon Calamari Shipyards|space battle]] was interrupted by the arrival of a Triumvirate fleet led by Val and [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Gar Stazi]].<ref name="Legacy 9" />

Solo took out enemy [[Droid/Legends|droids]] with the ship's laser cannons as one of Stazi's tankers, the ''[[Trand Cappa]]'', released [[Water/Legends|water]] into the [[Mon Calamari Orbital Shipyards]]. When two pirates opened one of the [[Shipyard/Legends|shipyards]]' bay doors, all of the freighter's crew save for AG-37 went aboard in order to prevent the Mon Calamari and [[Quarren/Legends|Quarren]] [[Refugee/Legends|refugees]] inside from being sucked into the [[Vacuum/Legends|vacuum]] of space. AG-37 continued to fly in the [[Space warfare/Legends|battle]], which was swiftly won by the Triumvirate fleet. AG-37 then committed both himself and his freighter to a [[Darth Wredd's insurgency|hunt for Darth Wredd]] that Solo, Assam, and the [[Imperial communications droid|comm droid]] had been undertaking, and Sauk joined as well.<ref name="Legacy 10" />

===Rescuing Ania===
[[File:AG-37_and_crew_unloading_supplies.jpg|thumb|right|250px|AG-37 and crew unloading goods]]
[[139 ABY|A year]] following the liberation of the Mon Calamari Shipyards, AG-37 did a delivery run to the [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]] [[Lasgo Port]], which was in a system that was surrounded by an orbital minefield left over from the Second Imperial Civil War. While visiting Lasgo Port, Ania discovered that she wanted by the Triumvirate authorities for the murder of the Imperial Knight [[Teemen Alton]], a crime which she denied committing. Shortly later, Ania was kidnapped by her former friend [[Ramid]] and his spacers. Ramid tricked Ania into boarding his freighter under the pretext of carrying out repairs and then disappeared with her into hyperspace. Ramid also attempted to detonate several nearby mines but Jao managed to move AG-37's freighter out of harm's way. During the kidnapping, AG-37's freighter sustained some light damage to its outer hull by laser fire from Ramid's starship, which was initially mistaken for meteor damage.<ref name="Legacy 11">[[Legacy (2013) 11|''Legacy'' (2013) 11]]</ref>

Following Ania's kidnapping, AG-37, Sauk, and Jao embarked on a quest to rescue Ania and to ascertain the truth about the charges against her. While Jao was suspicious about Ania, AG-37 and Sauk defended her and insisted that she did not murder the Imperial Knight. Their travels took them to a barren planet which rain glass and acid. Due to the inhospitable atmospheric conditions, Sauk and Jao remained aboard AG-37's freighter while AG-37 scouted the area for any sign of Ania and Ramid. During their wait, Sauk and Jao received a transmission from the Imperial Knight Yalta Val, who had found new evidence that Ania was innocent because the actual murderer, a [[Unidentified masked bounty hunter|mysterious bounty hunter]], had a prosthetic hand. By contrast, Ania was fully biological. After receiving further word that AG-37 had tracked down Ania and Ramid at a nearby settlement, Sauk and Jao flew the freighter towards that settlement.<ref name="Legacy 14">[[Legacy (2013) 14|''Legacy'' (2013) 14]]</ref>

While Sauk waited aboard AG-37's freighter, Jao traveled into the settlement to rescue Ania. By that stage, the mysterious bounty hunter had killed Ramid and had almost captured Ania. Following a long and protracted duel, Ania and Jao succeeded in killing the bounty hunter, who had intended to implant her prosthetic hand on Ania's left hand in order to frame her for Alton's murder. However, Ania's problems were not over yet since she was arrested by a squad of [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] and extradited to the galactic capital [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] to face trial. After recovering AG-37, whose mechanical body had been damaged during a downpour of acid rain, Jao and Sauk traveled to Coruscant to clear Ania's name. Despite securing Ania's acquittal and release, Jao Assam was arrested for deserting the Imperial Knights, a crime which carried the death penalty.<ref name="Legacy 15">[[Legacy (2013) 15|''Legacy'' (2013) 15]]</ref>

===The floating world and beyond===
[[File:Ania_commanding_Stormtroopers.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Ania and Stormtroopers in the freighter's cramped passenger quarters]]
After the rogue Sith Darth Wredd "kidnapped" Jao Assam and spirited him offworld, the [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Empress]] [[Marasiah Fel]] sent Ania and her companions on a mission to rescue Jao. She also assigned Ania a platoon of [[Trandoshan/Legends|Trandoshan]] stormtroopers as protective escorts. For this mission, Ania used AG-37's freighter. The freighter's accommodation was not too comfortable for the large stormtroopers. After receiving Jao Assam's coordinates, Ania and her companions traveled to the floating world of Mala.<ref name="Legacy 16" /> Unknown to them, Darth Wredd had planned to lure the Imperial Knights and the One Sith into a trap.<ref name="Legacy 17">[[Legacy (2013) 17|''Legacy'' (2013) 17]]</ref> He intended to avenge the destruction of his family and his homeworld by destroying the One Sith. Wredd also wanted to kill Empress Fel and bring Jao Assam to the dark side.<ref name="Legacy 18">[[Legacy (2013) 18|''Legacy'' (2013) 18]]</ref>

AG-37's freighter managed to land Ania's party on Mala's surface but did not participate in the [[Battle of the Floating World]], which saw the destruction of the One Sith and the death of Darth Wredd. Following the events on Mala, AG-37's freighter returned to Coruscant where it was refueled and had its supplies replenished. Jao Assam was also pardoned by Empress Fel and allowed to leave the Imperial Knights. He joined Ania and her companions on their travels across the galaxy on AG-37's freighter. [[140 ABY|A year later]], Sauk visited a cantina to buy a stabilizing coil. This purchase came at an opportune moment since Ania and her companions were immediately attacked by an unidentified party.<ref name="Legacy 18" />

==Behind the scenes==
AG-37's freighter debuted in [[Corinna Bechko]] and [[Gabriel Hardman]]'s ''[[Star Wars: Legacy Volume 2]]'' series, which ran from [[2013]] to [[2014]]. The starship was designed by [[Jimmy Presler]], drawn by Hardman and [[Brian Albert Thies]], and colored by [[Rachelle Rosenberg]] and [[Michael Heisler]]. In response to a fan query, the series' editor [[Randy Stradley]] confirmed that AG-37's freighter had not been modified into a smuggling vessel like Han Solo and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca's]] starship, the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']]. Stradley explained that while Solo and Chewbacca had operated outside the law, AG-37 operated within the law most of the time. To date, the ship has not been named.<ref name="SW L2 7 endnotes">[[Legacy (2013) 7|''Legacy'' (2013) 7]] endnotes.</ref>
